parts.text:
You encounter Diona at Barbeloth's fortune-telling booth...

#### Talk to Diona

**Diona:** ...So you can't help me fix this annoying affliction either?

**Barbeloth:** Precisely. It's already too deeply intertwined with your fate. Imagine your destiny is a tree — this "affliction" is like a new shoot growing from its branches.

**Barbeloth:** It's been helping you absorb sunlight and dew this whole time. It long ago began to shape your fate.

**Barbeloth:** If you cut it off now, the wound left behind might fester, infecting the entire tree.

**Diona:** Hmph... You make it sound like it's a good thing. It's clearly getting in my way, keeping me from mixing the drinks I need!

**Diona:** It's more like one of those vines that wrap around the trunks of giant trees — restricting their growth and slowly strangling them!

**Barbeloth:** Well, if that were the case, your fate would have rejected it, and we could have easily pruned it away... Unfortunately for you, it's not at all what you say it is.

**Barbeloth:** Alright, enough talk. That should be enough to convince you I'm a legitimate fortune teller, yes?

**Barbeloth:** Now, just like I told you, come here and pick a card at random, and let me give you a little advice about your future.

**Diona:** Hmm... So, I just pick one at random, hm? Okay... How about this one...? No, wait, this one...!

**Barbeloth:** Don't overthink it — no matter how you choose, you can only ever draw the card that's destined for you. Hahahaha...

**Diona:** (*shudder*... This fortune teller's laugh is so creepy! She's just like an old witch from a fairy tale!)

**Diona:** (But since she's so good at it, her advice could prove really helpful... I have to choose my card carefully!)

##### Response branch 1

- **Traveler:** You're scaring her.

##### Response branch 2

- **Traveler:** Long time no see, Diona.

##### Shared continuation

**Diona:** Huh? Traveler, Paimon?

**Barbeloth:** True to form, here you are at just the right moment.

##### Response branch 1

- **Traveler:** You're too kind.

##### Response branch 2

- **Traveler:** Timing is my strong suit.

##### Response branch 3

- **Traveler:** How else could I handle so many commissions?

##### Shared continuation

**Barbeloth:** Hahaha, well said. Compared to an intangible thing like Fate, commissions have a far more intuitive effect on shaping our words and deeds.

**Barbeloth:** Now, seeing as you're here, perhaps you could have a word with this little one? She doesn't seem very trusting of an old "witch" like me.

**Paimon:** Well, it's not so easy to trust a weird-looking fortune teller who's set up stall in the middle of nowhere...

**Diona:** (Traveler seems to know this fortune teller pretty well? Great, I can finally ask someone I trust...!)

**Diona:** ...Traveler, Paimon, come over here a second. I need to talk to you in private.

##### Response branch 1

- **Traveler:** I was just about to ask...

##### Response branch 2

- **Traveler:** What are you doing in Fontaine?

##### Shared continuation

**Diona:** Looking for new ingredients, of course! Hmph, my previous approach to mixing drinks was far too narrow-minded... I kept limiting myself to actual food...

**Paimon:** Uhm... Haha... Paimon wouldn't exactly call the things you put in your drinks "food," Diona...

**Diona:** Weeeell, it's all technically edible! As long as you grit your teeth and close your eyes, it's stuff you can force yourself to swallow.

##### Response branch 1

- **Traveler:** So, you're planning to find...

##### Response branch 2

- **Traveler:** Completely inedible ingredients?

##### Shared continuation

**Diona:** Exactly! ...I've already found a bunch of rusted screws, scrapped cables, coagulated chunks of grease, dustbunnies, toejam...

**Diona:** And it's all thanks to that guy from the Fontaine Research Institute who makes Fonta. He's been a real help!

##### Response branch 1

- **Traveler:** You know Heinry!?

##### Response branch 2

- **Traveler:** Where did you run into him?

##### Shared continuation

**Diona:** Well... I heard that really tasty fizzy drink stuff comes from the Fontaine Research Institute, so I headed over to take a look.

**Diona:** When I got there, Mr. Heinry let me try a few bottles of the new Fonta flavors. Completely on the house, haha!

**Diona:** Mr. Heinry doesn't smell of alcohol at all! Nope, he just smells like Fonta, sweet and tangy, haha. One sniff and you can tell he's a reliable sort of grown up.

**Diona:** Aaaand, he was the one who suggested I come to this stall. He said my affliction is probably beyond the Research Institute's ability to analyze.

**Diona:** But he heard that this weird fortune-teller who showed up recently near the Court of Fontaine. Apparently, everyone who's been here says she's crazy accurate!

**Diona:** "Maybe if you get your fortune told, you'll learn something about what's causing your affliction. If you grasp the principles behind it, perhaps you can find a cure."

**Paimon:** Well... Hard to argue with that logic! Guess he didn't end up becoming a researcher at the Fontaine Research Institute for nothing...

**Diona:** So, I came here to see the fortune-teller... As soon as I walked over, she stopped me and said there was a strange disturbance surrounding me.

**Diona:** Before I could ask, she blurted out all the answers to my questions, but...

**Barbeloth:** ...But the scientific logic of the Fontaine Research Institute doesn't directly apply to divination.

**Barbeloth:** Even if you understand the principles, it doesn't mean the solution will be easy to come by... Just like I told you.

**Barbeloth:** Mysticism isn't built of bearings and bolts, and I can't simply "repair" your fate for you.

**Diona:** Are you telling me nothing can be changed? Then what's the point of drawing a card...

**Barbeloth:** By drawing a card, you may just find a tiny missing gear to fit into the wheel of fate.

**Barbeloth:** It may seem insignificant, but when installed correctly, the tiniest gears can still drive massive mechanisms.

**Diona:** You... you're not just humoring me, are you? Traveler, what do you think...

##### Response branch 1

- **Traveler:** Barbeloth is very reliable.

##### Response branch 2

- **Traveler:** Just relax and draw a card.

##### Shared continuation

**Diona:** ...Alright, if you say so, then I'll take one...

Under Barbeloth's watchful gaze, Diona reaches out and slowly draws a Lunar Arcanum...

**Diona:** Alright, h—here we go. Looks like it's...

**Barbeloth:** ...Oh my, how strange... To think the disturbance surrounding you has grown with such vigor.

**Barbeloth:** It's no longer a shoot, but a sturdy branch. How curious...

**Diona:** Huh? W—What are you saying? Does... does this mean the drinks I mix will taste even better from now on!?

##### Response branch 1

- **Traveler:** That doesn't sound like a bad thing in itself...

##### Response branch 2

- **Traveler:** But given everything we know about Diona's motivations...

##### Shared continuation

**Barbeloth:** If we judge solely by your affliction, that would indeed be the case. Furthermore, the card you drew is the reversed High Priestess.

**Barbeloth:** Which means you've been too focused on the illusions before the veil. Which is precisely why you've been unable to pass through it for so long.

**Diona:** That doesn't sound like it has anything to do with mixing drinks... I thought this card would tell me what ingredients I need to use...

**Barbeloth:** Heh... The Lunar Arcana aren't known for creating recipes — at least not yet.

**Barbeloth:** But mixing drinks isn't the only way to find the answers you're looking for.

**Diona:** The answer is to teach those old boozehounds a lesson, so they never get drunk and cause trouble again.

**Barbeloth:** You're certainly driven. But while your body moves forward, your heart remains stuck.

**Diona:** That's not true! I... I hate those weird old drunkards from the bottom of my heart! Especially—

**Barbeloth:** Haha, I see. Then... have you talked to the one who fills your heart the most?

**Diona:** I... Uhm... H—How did you know I was thinking about one person in particular? I didn't even...

**Barbeloth:** Through divination, of course. Hehehe, perhaps you should cast aside your impatience and confused emotions, and tell him how you truly feel.

**Barbeloth:** You might find it more effective than trying to mix the most disgusting drinks in the world.

**Diona:** ...There's no way he'll listen. Once he's started drinking, he doesn't listen to anyone.

**Barbeloth:** Perhaps that was true before. But now, you've found a tiny gear from the wheel of fate. Returned to its rightful place, certain things might undergo... subtle changes.

**Diona:** You mean that? B-b-b-but it's just a card...

**Barbeloth:** Of course not that! I'm talking about your heart — something which has already begun to change.

**Diona:** M—My heart hasn't changed at all! Now... I need to go look for ingredients!

**Diona:** ...Uhm, how much is the divination fee? I can pay it in full.

**Barbeloth:** Oh my, what a well-mannered child. Much more endearing than that other little brat. But there's no need for a fee. Just consider this a gift from a witch.

**Diona:** Th—Thank you. If you ever come to Mondstadt... I can treat you to a drink. I guarantee it'll taste delicious.

**Barbeloth:** Mondstadt, you say? Yes... If I get the chance, that might not be such a terrible idea...

**Diona:** And thank you for helping me out, Traveler and Paimon.

##### Response branch 1

- **Traveler:** You're welcome!

##### Response branch 2

- **Traveler:** If you ever need help, just let me know.

##### Shared continuation

**Paimon:** No matter the trouble, Paimon and Traveler will swoop in and save the day!

**Paimon:** But swooping in is thirsty work, hehehe... So once we're done, we wouldn't say no to some of your tasty drinks, Diona!

**Diona:** ...It's a deal! Next time you're in Mondstadt, I'll treat you to the best drinks you've ever tasted — the kind with absolutely zippo alcohol!

**Barbeloth:** By the way, if you have any more questions about your card, look for someone named Mona. You probably already know who I'm talking about?

**Diona:** Mona? Yeah, I know her! She always orders the cheapest drinks. Is she a powerful fortune teller, too?

**Barbeloth:** Hah, she's nowhere near my level. Still, she should be up to the task of reading the Lunar Arcana — otherwise, she might as well hang up her hat.

**Barbeloth:** Just tell her you've brought a prophecy on behalf of the Mighty Astromancer Barbeloth Trismegistus — as a test.

**Barbeloth:** Don't worry. As long as you say that, she'll do her best to interpret it for you.

**Diona:** Mmhmm, I think I got that! Astro... mancer... Barbeloth Trismegistus... Meows, that's a long name...

**Diona:** Come to think of it, isn't Mona's name really long, too? I think it was... the Astrolo... What was it again?

#### Listen to Diona's story...
